title: A thickening of an affine scheme is affine
statement: Let $i:X\to X'$ be a thickening of schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], i.e. a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] that is surjective on underlying topological spaces (no finite order hypothesis). If $X$ is an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], then $X'$ is an affine scheme.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 06AD (label lemma-thickening-affine-scheme); Stacks proves it as a special case of Limits, Proposition 05YU (label proposition-affine: a scheme receiving a surjective universally closed morphism from an affine scheme is affine), a closed immersion being universally closed; the finite order case is EGA I, Proposition 5.1.9, with a second proof in Stacks by Serre's criterion

proof.text: ($i$ is surjective and universally closed.) By definition of a thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $i:X\to X'$ is a closed immersion whose map of underlying topological spaces is surjective, i.e. $i$ is a surjective morphism of schemes [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. A closed immersion is universally closed [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc, clause (d)] in the sense of [def-weil-proper-morphism]. (This is the fact Stacks leaves implicit when it calls 06AD 'a special case' of 05YU.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 06AD (lemma-thickening-affine-scheme), first proof: 'This is a special case of Limits, Proposition 05YU'

proof.text: ($X'$ is affine.) Apply Limits, Proposition 05YU [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-affine-target] to the morphism $f:=i:X\to S:=X'$: its source $X$ is affine by hypothesis, and $i$ is surjective and universally closed by step 1. Hence $X'$ is an affine scheme.
